findings.detail: UserCreate exposed a role field and UserService.register persisted user_in.role for every user after the first, so POST /api/v1/auth/register with role=admin minted an administrator with access to every CurrentAdmin endpoint including user administration and conversation export. Fixed 2026-08-20: the field is removed from the schema (extra keys are ignored at the boundary), and role is now a keyword-only parameter of register() supplied only by trusted code (CLI user create/create-admin); the public route always registers role=user. Regression tests cover the service, the trusted CLI path, and the API boundary.

ConversationService.list_messages accepted a user_id but never passed it into get_conversation, and add_message took no actor at all, so any authenticated user who learned another conversation UUID could read its messages or inject user/assistant/system messages into it — active cross-conversation prompt injection into the owner's agent history, not merely disclosure. Fixed 2026-08-20: both methods route the acting user through get_conversation's ownership/share check (404 for strangers), and add_message additionally requires an edit share (403 for view-only recipients). Admin routes and internal agent persistence remain deliberately unscoped via user_id=None; the WebSocket user-turn persistence now passes the actor as defense in depth.

Pre-existing and surfaced by this session's adversarial review: get_conversation's share branch accepts any share row without inspecting share.permission, and update_conversation, archive_conversation, and delete_conversation authorize through it, so a view-only share recipient can rename, archive, or hard-delete the owner's conversation. The purpose-built ConversationShareService.check_edit_permission has zero callers. Link-share tokens are not affected (get_share matches shared_with, which is NULL for link shares). add_message was made permission-aware in this change. Fixed 2026-08-20 in the follow-up session (Require edit shares for conversation update/archive and restrict delete to owners): update_conversation and archive_conversation now authorize through get_conversation(require_edit=True) so a view-only share 403s, delete_conversation passes a new require_owner flag that rejects every share tier, and the orphaned check_edit_permission was deleted in favor of the single get_conversation primitive. Admin and internal callers keep the deliberate user_id=None trusted path. Six regression tests cover view and edit shares across all three write paths.
